procedure.description: insertion of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator with transvenous lead

denial.carcText: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer.
denial.text: Prairie Commons Medicaid Plan denied the claim for CPT 33249 (insertion of implantable cardioverter-defibrillator with transvenous lead) with date of service 2026-05-09. CARC 50: These are non-covered services because this is not deemed a 'medical necessity' by the payer. Payer remark: Documentation does not establish an ejection fraction of 35 percent or less after an adequate trial of guideline-directed medical therapy.

criteria.text: Left ventricular ejection fraction of 35 percent or less on echocardiography, nuclear study, or cardiac MRI, measured after at least 90 days of guideline-directed medical therapy.
New York Heart Association class II or III heart failure symptoms.

At least 90 days of guideline-directed medical therapy including a beta blocker and an ACE inhibitor, ARB, or ARNI, with a mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist and an SGLT2 inhibitor as tolerated, at maximally tolerated doses.
More than 40 days after any myocardial infarction and more than 90 days after any coronary revascularization.
Expected survival with good functional status of more than one year.

chart.text: A1c came back 6.8. Prediabetic range, same as last year. Walking program, cut the soda, recheck in six months. He is motivated.
Blood pressure check. 137 over 76 today, 120 over 92 on repeat. He has been taking the lisinopril 10 most days, admits to missing weekends. Low salt talk again. Keep the dose, recheck in 6 weeks.

Knee pain going down stairs, right side, no injury, no locking or giving way. Patellar grind positive, no effusion, ligaments stable. Patellofemoral pain. Quad strengthening sheet, ice after activity, cushioned shoes.
From the referring physician: please evaluate and treat as you see fit. We have exhausted what we can do in primary care and the patient is motivated. Recent labs enclosed, all within normal limits.

Here with a cough and congestion for 4 days, low grade temp at home, no shortness of breath. Lungs clear, throat a little red, ears fine. Looks viral. Fluids, rest, honey for the cough, come back if he gets a fever over 101 or it goes past two weeks.
Optometry report forwarded for the record. Routine refraction, mild astigmatism, new glasses prescribed, retinas healthy, pressures 18 and 16. No ocular pathology noted.

62 year old man in cardiology clinic for ischemic cardiomyopathy after his infarction. Reviewed the plan: optimize medications, repeat the echo in 3 months, and decide on a defibrillator then. He understands the device is for sudden death prevention, not symptoms. His history otherwise: anxiety, sees a counselor. Allergies: codeine makes him sick. Never smoked, occasional beer, lives alone. Family history noncontributory for what we are talking about today. Anterior ST-elevation infarction 12 months ago, drug-eluting stent to the proximal left anterior descending at that time. No revascularization since; no residual ischemia on the follow-up stress study. No other life-limiting illness, independent, still working. Expected survival well over a year.
Transthoracic echocardiogram. Left ventricular ejection fraction 27 percent by biplane Simpson’s, anterior and apical akinesis, mild mitral regurgitation, no thrombus.

Carvedilol 25 twice daily, sacubitril-valsartan 97/103 twice daily, spironolactone 25 daily, empagliflozin 10 daily. All four started after the infarction and titrated to these doses by the second cardiology visit; doses unchanged since.
Dermatology consult note received. Two actinic keratoses on the forehead treated with cryotherapy. Annual skin check recommended, sunscreen counseling done.
Message from the patient about scheduling. Wants a date in the next couple of months if the insurance comes through. Passed to the scheduler.
Thyroid labs back. TSH 3.5, free T4 normal. No change to the levothyroxine 50. Repeat in a year.
He called asking about travel vaccines for a trip in the spring. Advised hepatitis A and a typhoid booster, referred to the travel clinic. Nothing else needed from us.
Seasonal allergies acting up, itchy eyes, sneezing, clear drainage, worse outdoors. No wheeze. Cetirizine at night and the saline rinse. Fine with that.

Low back strain after moving furniture over the weekend. No radiation down the legs, no numbness, no bowel or bladder trouble. Paraspinal tenderness, straight leg raise negative. Heat, keep moving, ibuprofen with food for a week. Should settle.
Pharmacy called about the refill on the omeprazole 40. Approved 90 days. He mentioned the heartburn is better since cutting back on coffee.
Patient called about a tick bite on the shoulder after a hike. Tick removed whole, no rash, no fever. Watch for a bull's-eye rash or flu symptoms over the next month and call if either shows up.
Burning with urination for two days, going frequently, no fever, no back pain. Urine dip positive for leukocytes and nitrites. Nitrofurantoin for five days, push fluids, call if fever or flank pain.

Trouble sleeping for a couple of months, falls asleep fine but wakes at three and lies there. No snoring per the spouse, no daytime naps, two cups of coffee before noon. Went over sleep hygiene, no screens in bed, cut the afternoon caffeine. Will hold off on medication for now.

Mole on the left forearm that his spouse noticed. About 4 millimeters, even color, regular border, no change he is aware of. Looks benign. Photo in the chart for comparison, recheck in a year or sooner if it changes.
Check-in while we wait on the insurance. No change in the complaints. Reviewed the risks and recovery one more time, he remains sure about going ahead.
Work note requested for a sick day last Tuesday. Faxed to the employer.
Vitamin D came back 24. Started 2000 units daily, recheck in three months. Also talked about calcium from food rather than pills.

Three-month visit. Reviewed the repeat echocardiogram with him. Discussed primary prevention defibrillator, risks of implant, what a shock feels like, driving rules. Decision made today. Vitals today 137 over 81, pulse 81. Short of breath carrying groceries up one flight, fine on the flat, no orthopnea now. Class II to III. 94 days on full guideline-directed therapy at target doses, tolerating, potassium 4.4, blood pressure 108 over 64.

Repeat transthoracic echocardiogram after 3 months of optimized medical therapy. Left ventricular ejection fraction 27 percent by biplane Simpson’s, unchanged. Persistent anterior and apical akinesis.

Called his with the cholesterol results. Total 211, LDL 131, HDL 45, triglycerides 143. Discussed diet and walking. He wants to try lifestyle first for six months before we talk about a statin. Agreed.
Pre-procedure visit for device implant. Hold the apixaban one dose, continue the rest. Chest X-ray and labs fine. Consent signed.

expected.note: The chart documents every criterion; the CARC 50 denial can be answered from the record.
